verses.29: Woe to the bloody city, all lies, full of plunder, whose looting never stops!
verses.30: The crack of the whip, the rumbling sounds of wheels; horses a-gallop, chariots bounding,
verses.31: Cavalry charging, The flame of the sword, the flash of the spear, the many slain, the heaping corpses, the endless bodies to stumble upon!
verses.32: For the many debaucheries of the harlot, fair and charming, a mistress of witchcraft, Who enslaved nations with her harlotries, and peoples by her witchcraft:
verses.33: I am come against you, and I will strip your skirt from you; I will show your nakedness to the nations, to the kingdoms your shame!
verses.34: I will cast filth upon you, disgrace you and put you to shame;
verses.35: Till everyone who sees you runs from you, saying, "Nineveh is destroyed; who can pity her? Where can one find any to console her?"
verses.36: Are you better than No-amon that was set among the streams, Surrounded by waters, with the flood for her rampart and water her wall?
verses.37: Ethiopia was her strength, and Egypt, and others without end; Put and the Libyans were her auxiliaries.
verses.38: Yet even she went captive into exile, even her little ones were dashed to pieces at the corner of every street; For her nobles they cast lots, and all her great men were put into chains.
verses.39: You too, shall drink of this till you faint away; you, too, shall seek a refuge from the foe.
verses.40: All your fortresses are but fig trees, bearing early figs That fall, when shaken, into the hungry mouth.
verses.41: See, the troops are women in your midst; to your foes the gates of your land are open wide, fire has consumed their bars.
verses.42: Draw water for the siege, strengthen your fortresses; Go down into the mud and tread the clay, take hold of the brick mold!
verses.43: There the fire shall consume you, the sword shall cut you down. Multiply like the grasshoppers, multiply like the locusts!
verses.44: Make your couriers more numerous than the stars,
verses.45: your garrisons as many as grasshoppers, And your scribes as locust swarms gathered on the rubble fences on a cold day! Yet when the sun warms them, the grasshoppers will spread their wings and fly, and vanish, no one knows where.
verses.46: Alas! how your shepherds slumber, O king of Assyria, your nobles have gone to rest; Your people are scattered upon the mountains, with none to gather them.
verses.47: There is no healing for your hurt, your wound is mortal. All who hear this news of you clap their hands over you; For who has not been overwhelmed, steadily, by your malice?
